description: Backend improvements: enhance ML preprocessing (CLAHE, gamma, sharpening, noise reduction), strengthen crack validation (stricter thresholds, DJI UI rejection, adaptive confidence), improve system stability (thread watchdog, auto-recovery, error resilience), and replace LetsView mss capture with Windows Graphics Capture API stub.
steps: 1. In inference_core.py, add a preprocess_frame() function before YOLO inference that applies: (a) CLAHE on the L channel of LAB color space, (b) gamma correction (gamma=1.2), (c) light unsharp mask sharpening, (d) bilateral filter for noise reduction while preserving edges. Call this in annotate_frame() before model.predict().
2. In inference_core.py, raise the default confidence threshold from 0.25 to 0.40 in annotate_frame() function signature. Also update app.py CONF default from 0.25 to 0.40.

3. In crack_validator.py, add DJI UI rejection: detect if the frame contains common DJI Fly interface elements by checking for high-contrast rectangular regions in the top/bottom 15% of the frame (typical UI overlay zones). Add a filter that rejects detections whose bounding box falls entirely within these UI zones. Increase MIN_CRACK_AREA_PX from 100 to 150, MIN_CRACK_LENGTH_PX from 20 to 30, and MIN_ASPECT_RATIO from 2.0 to 2.5.

4. In detector.py, add a watchdog mechanism: wrap the _run() loop body in a try/except that catches all exceptions, logs them, sleeps 1 second, and continues. Add a _restart_count counter. If the video source fails more than 5 times in 30 seconds, increase reconnect cooldown to 5 seconds. Add heartbeat tracking (last_frame_time) so external code can detect if the detector is stuck.

5. In capture_manager.py, add similar resilience: wrap _capture_worker in a broader try/except/finally that always resets _capture_in_progress. Add a timeout mechanism - if _capture_worker takes more than 30 seconds, the state is force-reset to monitoring. Increase VERIFICATION_FRAME_COUNT from 5 to 5 (keep same) but add a requirement that frames must span at least 1.5 seconds (not just 5 consecutive frames that could all arrive in <1s).

6. Replace letsview_source.py implementation: keep the same LetsViewSource class interface (open/read/release/is_open) but replace the mss-based capture with Windows Graphics Capture API using winsdk package. The new implementation should: (a) find LetsView window by HWND using ctypes/win32, (b) create a GraphicsCaptureItem from the HWND, (c) use Direct3D11CaptureFramePool for frame capture, (d) continue capturing even if the window is covered or partially offscreen. On non-Windows or if winsdk is not available, fall back gracefully (open() returns False). Add 'winsdk' to requirements.txt as an optional dependency with a comment.
7. In requirements.txt, remove PyGetWindow and mss (no longer needed since letsview_source.py will use winsdk). Add winsdk>=1.0 with a comment that it is Windows-only and optional.

8. Update tests/test_integration.py: adjust any test that references the old confidence default (0.25) to use 0.40. Add a test for the new preprocess_frame() function (create a dark frame, verify CLAHE brightens it). Add a test verifying DJI UI zone rejection in crack_validator.
acceptance_criteria: inference_core.annotate_frame() applies CLAHE+gamma+sharpening+noise reduction before inference
Default confidence threshold is 0.40 in both inference_core.py and app.py
crack_validator rejects detections in DJI UI zones (top/bottom 15% of frame)
crack_validator thresholds are stricter: MIN_CRACK_AREA_PX=150, MIN_CRACK_LENGTH_PX=30, MIN_ASPECT_RATIO=2.5
detector.py has try/except resilience in the main loop with automatic recovery
letsview_source.py uses winsdk-based Windows Graphics Capture API with graceful fallback
requirements.txt updated (removed mss/PyGetWindow, added winsdk as optional)
